claim.quote: We present first results after successfully running the prototype detector for a period of about 15 months in the Gran Sasso Underground Laboratory. We analyze the results in terms of limits on WIMP-nucleon cross sections

name: First Results from the Heidelberg Dark Matter Search Experiment
notes: The numerical limit is shown only in a figure of the paper; the abstract gives no value, so no key value is recorded.

summary.plain: After about 15 months in the Gran Sasso laboratory the HDMS prototype, two nested germanium crystals, gave its first limits on how strongly dark matter particles can interact with ordinary nuclei.
summary.technical: Prototype with natural Ge crystals (inner 202 g, outer 2111 g); the last 49 days (9.9 kg d) analysed without background subtraction; spin-independent WIMP-nucleon limits better than Heidelberg-Moscow below about 40 GeV thanks to a 2 keV threshold (body of the paper; the abstract states only that limits are derived).

title: First Results from the Heidelberg Dark Matter Search Experiment
why_it_matters: One of the first low-threshold germanium limits that did not rely on background subtraction, and the proof of the nested-crystal idea before the enriched-73Ge final setup.
